This is like the way the earth is called "the mother of people," because it shelters them, and as ʿUtbah ibn Abī Sufyān said in war: "We are its sons and it is our mother." So Allah, Exalted is He, made the Abyss the mother of the disbeliever, since it is his dwelling. Others said: it is an expression of optimism for evil, with a figurative usage, as they say: "his mother is bereaved" (ʿummuhu thākil) and "his star has fallen" (hawā najmuhu). Abū Ṣāliḥ and others said: the intended meaning is the mother of his head, because they fall on their heads. Ṭalḥah read: "fa-ummuhu" with a kasra on the hamza and a damma on the mim, doubled.

Then Exalted is He established His Prophet ﷺ in knowledge of its matter and its magnitude, then informed him that it is a blazing Fire. Ibn Isḥāq and al-Aʿmash read: "mā hiyah" with the dropping of the hā' in continuous speech. Al-Mubarrad narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said to a man: "May you have no mother (lā umma laka)!" The man said: O Messenger of Allah, you call me to guidance and say, "May you have no mother"? He said: "I only mean, may you have no Fire (lā nāra laka)." Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿his refuge will be the Abyss﴾.

The commentary on al-Qāriʿah is complete, and praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on Surah al-Qari'ah

It is Makkan without any disagreement.

The Exalted and Majestic said:

﴿The Striking Calamity!﴾ ﴿What is the Striking Calamity?﴾ ﴿And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?﴾ ﴿It is a Day when mankind will be like scattered moths,﴾ ﴿and the mountains will be like carded wool.﴾ ﴿As for him whose scales are heavy,﴾ ﴿he will be in a pleasant life.﴾ ﴿But as for him whose scales are light,﴾ ﴿his refuge will be the Abyss.﴾ ﴿And what will make you know what it is?﴾ ﴿A blazing Fire.﴾

ʿĪsā read "al-qāriʿatu, mā al-qāriʿatu" with the accusative (naṣb). The majority of the exegetes said: al-Qāriʿah is the Resurrection itself, because it strikes the hearts with its terror. Some of the early interpreters said: al-Qāriʿah is the blast of the trumpet (ṣayḥat al-nafkhah) in the Ṣūr, because it strikes the ears, and within that, the hearts. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And what will make you know﴾ is an exaltation of its matter, and a similar expression has already passed.

"Yawma" is an adverb of time (ẓarf), and its governing element (ʿāmil) is "al-qāriʿah". Abū ʿAmr inclined (imālah) "al-qāriʿata". "Al-farrāsh" is a small bird that falls into the fire and keeps aiming for it; it continually throws itself at the lamp and the like until it burns. From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "I am holding you back by your waistbands from the Fire, while you are rushing into it like the rushing of the moths and the locusts." Al-Farrā' said: "al-Firāsh" in the verse is the swarm of young locusts, which spreads over the earth and the air. "Al-mabthūth" here means: scattered in its individual parts, though its totality is present and connected. Some scholars said: At the beginning of their rising from the graves, people are like scattered moths, because they come and go without order; then the caller calls them and they turn towards the place of gathering (al-maḥshar), so at that time they are like the spreading locusts, because locusts are always directed towards a specific destination.

The linguists differed concerning "al-ʿihn". It was said: it is wool in general. It was said: it is red wool. It was said: it is wool of various colours. Those who held this view cited the verse of Zuhayr:

"As if the crumbs of ʿihn in every dwelling-place they alighted in were the seeds of al-Fanā, unbroken."

Al-Fanā is the fox-grape (ʿinab al-thaʿlab), and its seed before being broken is green, red and yellow. Likewise the mountains have streaks of white, red, yellow and black, so the comparison is fitting. The mountains being like ʿihn applies only before the time of their crumbling, before being blown away, and their being brought down here, in levels. "Al-nafsh" is the loosening of the parts and their separation from being compacted. In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn Jubayr: "ka-al-ṣūf al-manfūsh" (like the carded wool).

"Al-mawāzīn" are those of the Resurrection. The majority of the scholars, jurists and traditionists said: the Scale of the Resurrection has a pillar and two pans, so that Allah, Exalted is He, may make clear the matter of the servants through what they know and are certain of. Mujāhid said: There is no scale there; rather, it is justice, a parable expressed through the scale, since it is the most just thing people know. The scales are referred to in plural for a person because he has many different weighable deeds. Its heaviness is through faith and good deeds, and its lightness is through their absence and scarcity. The scale of a believer will never be light with the lightness that destroys.

"ʿĪshatin rāḍiyah" means: one characterised by contentment (dhāt riḍan), with the relative form (ʿalā al-nasab). This is the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. As for His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿his refuge will be the Abyss﴾, many of the exegetes said: the intended meaning of "the mother" is the Abyss itself, and it is the lowest level of the Fire to which whoever is made to know it is sent down. This is like the way the earth is called "the mother of people," because it shelters them, and as ʿUtbah ibn Abī Sufyān said in war: "We are its sons and it is our mother." So Allah, Exalted is He, made the Abyss the mother of the disbeliever, since it is his dwelling. Others said: it is an expression of optimism for evil, with a figurative usage, as they say: "his mother is bereaved" (ʿummuhu thākil) and "his star has fallen" (hawā najmuhu). Then Exalted is He established His Prophet ﷺ in knowledge of its matter and its magnitude, then informed him that it is a blazing Fire. The man said: O Messenger of Allah, you call me to guidance and say, "May you have no mother"? He said: "I only mean, may you have no Fire (lā nāra laka)."
